implementation.key_insight: The kernel does collide(BB(stream(f))), not BB(stream(collide(f))). Collision happens AFTER bounce-back.
features: Periodic boundary conditions on all axes

single_step_test.test_method: Comparison against production PyTorch chain (stream3d + bounce_back_cells_3d + collide_advanced_3d)

performance.note: Performance benchmark not available in this environment (no CUDA device)
performance.rationale: Pure PyTorch operations are vectorized and avoid Triton interpreter overhead. On GPU with native CUDA, should achieve significant speedup over interpret mode.

regression_tests.note: Full regression tests require CUDA device
verified: No breaking changes to existing API

limitations: CM (cascaded central moments) collision uses simplified BGK-like relaxation (TODO: full implementation)
Force computation uses f_streamed (pre-bounce-back) which matches kernel semantics

usage_example.code:
from tensorlbm.triton_fused_obstacle import torch_fused_obstacle_xfar_les

# Pure PyTorch path (no Triton required)
f_out = torch_fused_obstacle_xfar_les(
    f,           # (19, nz, ny, nx) distribution
    nu_lb=0.005, # viscosity
    obstacle,    # (nz, ny, nx) int8 mask
    Cs=0.0,      # Smagorinsky constant (0 = no LES)
    delta=1.0,   # LES filter width
    collision='BGK'
)
usage_example.notes: Drop-in replacement for triton_fused_obstacle_xfar_les with identical semantics
